text_simplified:
Ibn al-Qayyim (may Allah have mercy on him) observed that a child's dutifulness to his parent generally arises from the parent's fairness among his children, whereas disobedience and rebellion often stem from a parent's unfairness and favoritism.
Parents must therefore beware of injustice and favoring some children over others.
Alongside fairness comes gentleness, leniency, and good speech in raising children.

review_defects.why: The Arabic title includes 'الانتقال إلى ركيزة الرفق' (transition to the pillar of gentleness), but the English replaces this with 'the Importance of Gentleness,' dropping the structural transition.
The Arabic title references transitioning to 'the pillar of gentleness' (ركيزة الرفق), a structural concept in the series; the English drops both 'transition' and 'pillar'.
The Arabic presents cultivating gentleness as a parallel parental duty («مع التحلي»), whereas the English phrasing makes gentleness sound like a natural accompaniment of fairness.
